structural_epochs.condition: The initial cutoff-safe panel contains four listed-consolidated issuers with recorded FY2016 statutory reports spanning room air conditioning, refrigeration/washing and multi-category appliance systems; this is a source-coverage state, not a peer-performance ranking.

At the later cutoff, FY2017 statutory reports remain available for the diversified appliance, refrigeration/washing and dual white-goods issuer boundaries; cross-company comparison still requires product, customer, channel and accounting-boundary matching.

Official cutoff context: The common environment was not a uniform white-goods volume path: category mix and capacity/utilisation exposure could differ before any company-specific conclusion is drawn.; A growing aggregate profit pool can coexist with absorption/friction risk; the future industry thesis must distinguish aggregate accounting growth from company-level sell-through, inventory and cash conversion.; The demand/channel backdrop was supportive in aggregate but channel migration could distribute its benefit unequally across companies and categories.; The category-specific label regime can affect the product/mix and channel questions that must be verified at company level, but the published catalogue alone does not measure a company's costs, product mix or customer response.
observations: The industry entered late 2018 with materially faster room-air-conditioner production than refrigerator and washing-machine production.
Aggregate appliance revenue and profit grew while the production-sales rate was below the prior-year level.
Broad appliance retail was growing and online physical-goods retail expanded faster in the same period.
The Pack's principal household-appliance categories were within a common energy-efficiency-label product regime before the Pack cutoff.
